_note: Declared physical section-order convention for docs/agent-memory/notebooks/*.md, read by scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh's same-day/tied-heading tie-break (FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-SAMEDAY-TIE-DROPS-NEWEST). The hook derives a notebook's convention AUTOMATICALLY from that file's OWN distinguishable (non-tied) section timestamps first — this table is consulted ONLY when a file's own headings give zero distinguishing signal (every retained '## ' section normalizes to the identical lossy 17-char key, e.g. 3+ same-day date-only headings written in one day). Do NOT add an entry for a notebook whose heading format normally carries sub-day precision (ISO timestamp, c<NNN> counter, cycle-N) — the auto-derivation already handles those correctly and a redundant override risks drifting stale. Add an entry ONLY after confirming the file's real physical convention via `git log -1 -p --unified=0 -- docs/agent-memory/notebooks/<file>.md` (does the newest cycle's own new section land at the TOP of the diff, i.e. prepended, or at the BOTTOM, i.e. appended) — see notebook-auto-prune.test.sh T5/T6 for the reference method. STATUS UPDATE (FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-DIRECTION-UNRESOLVABLE-ZERO-TS-NOTEBOOKS, 2026-07-31, AC-2): this table is now OPTIONAL, never load-bearing — the derivation NEVER dead-ends without it. A file with no entry here (and no distinguishing signal of its own) now resolves via a documented, deterministic default (newest_first: drop the physically-last tied section) instead of refusing to prune forever; see notebook-auto-prune.sh's direction case-statement default arm. This table remains useful ONLY as a manually-verified precision override for a specific known file where the default would pick the wrong direction (e.g. dev-frontend.md/dev-mcp-server.md below are genuinely oldest_first, the opposite of the default) — it is intentionally NOT grown one file at a time for every notebook that happens to hit the zero-signal case (feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist); the general case is now handled without it.
_maintained_by: developer or architect, MANUALLY, on an as-needed basis ONLY when the safe default (newest_first) is confirmed wrong for a specific file via the git log -1 -p method above — there is intentionally NO automated producer/flow step: safely deciding prepend-vs-append requires a human reading real git history (the exact method this table's own _note prescribes), and a wrong automated entry would silently invert the drop direction (the precise data-loss class this whole mechanism exists to prevent) — worse than the table simply having no entry, which is now a fully safe, resolving state.
